  • When fewer than 2 bootstrap replicates succeed, the fit is returned with NA standard errors and a warning, instead of an error.

  • Documentation now matches the implementation: the NB2 PMF uses size 1/alpha (as the variance and the code do); the PLL regression mean is exp(X beta + sigma^2 / 2) with the corresponding variance; the PLL integral uses the Poisson-Lindley scale lambda, not the mean; the PL regression section gives the base PMF evaluated at lambda (the expanded formula had the wrong power of theta + 2) and no longer describes an LR test against Poisson; the PGE integral is over the generalized-exponential distribution. Fitted objects record the package version that created them (model$fcr_version).

  • Packaging: DESCRIPTION has BugReports and the GitHub URL; a CITATION file and a contributor guide with a release checklist were added; CI also checks the minimum R version; the slowest stochastic tests are skipped on CRAN.

  • The minimum R version is now 4.5.0, because the current CRAN release of the gsl package (an import) requires it. ## Bug fixes (distribution functions and inputs)

  • pcom() ignored lower.tail and log.p. Both tails are now summed directly on the log scale with a precise normalizing constant, so upper tails are never negative and keep their relative precision (e.g. pcom(25, lambda = 1, nu = 1, lower.tail = FALSE) equals the Poisson value 9.5e-28). Recycling of mu, lambda and nu in dcom(), pcom() and qcom() follows the base-R rule (length 1 or the length of the first argument; other lengths are an error).

  • dpoisweibull() and friends used lambda inconsistently between the PMF and the mean; parameters given only partly now warn instead of failing.

  • The d/p/q functions of the Poisson-Lindley, Poisson-Lindley-Lognormal, Poisson-inverse-Gaussian, Poisson-inverse-gamma, Poisson-generalized- exponential, Sichel and inverse-gamma distributions return NaN (with one warning) for invalid parameters instead of failing, returning 0, or emitting extra warnings. Missing inputs give NA.

  • qsichel() returns Inf at p = 1 (it returned NA with a coercion warning) and NaN for p outside [0, 1] (it searched 10,000 counts). rsichel() and rinvgamma() accept a vector n (its length is used, as in base R).

  • halton_dists() draws one dimension by default, uses the stated half-width for uniform draws (mean +/- sdev), and errors for an unknown distribution. corr_haltons() gives each column its own mean, standard deviation and bounds for truncated normal draws, and errors for an unsupported distribution, hdraws with the wrong number of columns, or a Cholesky factor of the wrong size.

  • confint(), summary() and tidy() work (with NA standard errors) when a model has no covariance matrix.

  • bootstraps is checked up front (a single number of at least 2) instead of failing after the model is fit.

  • Data preparation rejects infinite counts and non-numeric (e.g. factor) responses, expands . in formulas, and keeps the contrasts of factors in auxiliary formulas for prediction. Fitted objects store the expanded formulas, so bootstrap refits of models written with . work.

  • method = "Nelder-Mead" is accepted by every estimator as an alias of "NM".

  • qplind() and qplindLnorm() return NA for missing parameters instead of failing, and qplindLnorm()/rplindLnorm() accept sigma = 0 (the Poisson-Lindley limit).

  • regCompTable() fits the baseline model only when the pseudo-R^2 is requested. tidy() classifies parameters from the model’s bookkeeping (covariates named like distribution parameters are no longer misclassified).

Documentation

  • The pkgdown site renders mathematics with MathJax (template: math-rendering: mathjax). The equations of help pages (\eqn{}, \deqn{}) and articles were shown as raw LaTeX, for example in ?countreg_mix.

  • The package description (DESCRIPTION) now summarizes the current scope: the 28 count families and their distribution functions, distribution-parameter, zero, underreporting, random-parameter, random-effects and finite-mixture models, the prediction, interval, effect and diagnostic tools, and references for latent-class regression, randomized quantile residuals and rootograms.

  • Corrected the parameter table in ?countreg (PGE, Sichel), the Poisson-Lindley-Lognormal mean and parameter descriptions, the RENB density, the Sichel reference (Zou, Lord and Zhang, 2012) and several typos. ?countreg no longer claims that an LR test is printed; see regCompTest().

  • ?countreg_rp documents each random-parameter distribution’s scale, the heterogeneity specification and the lognormal caveat.

  • ?renb states that the marginal variance exists only for a > 2 (it is infinite for the legal values 1 < a <= 2).

  • ?washington_roads describes the panel structure; the Rollover label in the data is corrected. The README function list is corrected and completed.

Other changes

  • Dependencies: broom, dplyr, modelr, purrr, stringr and tidyr are no longer used; generics is added. Whole-namespace imports are replaced by importFrom(). lamW stays in Suggests (its uses in qlindley() and lognormal random-parameter predictions are checked with rlang::check_installed()); dials and parsnip are added to Suggests.

  • rlindley() draws from the gamma mixture form directly (no longer needs lamW) and no longer warns for every whole-number n.

  • src/Makevars and src/Makevars.win are removed (no OpenMP or BLAS is used), so SystemRequirements: GNU make is dropped.

  • Added an R CMD check GitHub Actions workflow (including a job with only the hard dependencies installed) and a grouped pkgdown reference index. Removed the commented-out tests/testthat/test-all.R and a duplicated test.

  • The poilog engine is checked with rlang::check_installed().

  • msg1 and .dpge_one are no longer exported. The hand-maintained Collate field is removed.

Other new features

  • New margEffTable(): average marginal effects, elasticities and, for indicators, pseudo-elasticities or discrete changes, for every estimator, with delta-method or bootstrap (independent units, optional cluster_var) standard errors. Variables that change the expected count only through auxiliary formulas (underreporting, zero model, random parameters and their heterogeneity, and distribution parameters when the mean depends on them, as in hurdle models) are included by default.

  • New panel estimators repois() (random-effects Poisson) and negmultinom() (negative multinomial NM1, NM2 and NM-P), with weights, robust and bootstrap standard errors, predictions and the common methods.

  • Zero-inflated and hurdle models for every countreg() family, through the new zero_formula and zero_type arguments (checked against pscl::zeroinfl() and pscl::hurdle()).

  • predict(type = "prob") (probabilities of each count), randomized quantile residuals (residuals(type = "quantile")) and rootogram().

  • Analytic gradients for the Poisson, NB1 and NB2 families (with or without a dispersion formula), used by the gradient-based optimizers and by robust standard errors.

  • Internally, each count family is defined once in a family registry (R/families.R), which makes adding a family a one-file change.

  • predict(method = "Individual") (alias "EB") for countreg_rp() models now computes Empirical Bayes observation-specific predictions following Wood and Gayah (2025), weighting each draw by the likelihood of the unit’s observed outcomes. Previously it returned the simulated predictions. Panels are matched to the rows of newdata by id (a group_var given as a vector is stored as the column .fcr_panel_id), and the response expression is evaluated as in estimation. eb_type = "mean" returns the conditional mean instead of plugging in the conditional coefficients; the conditional coefficients and their standard deviations are returned as attributes.

  • predict() gains type = c("response", "true", "prob_reported", "link") for countreg() models.

  • countreg() accepts weights as a numeric vector as well as a column name.

Deprecations

  • countreg.rp() is deprecated; use countreg_rp(), now the documented name (?countreg_rp). countreg.rp() still works, with a once-per-session warning, and returns the same fit.
  • predict(object, data = ...) is deprecated; use newdata.
  • print.level in renb() and poisLind.re() is deprecated; use verbose. panel_id in countreg_rp() is deprecated; use group_var. The old names still work, with a once-per-session warning.

Methods and API consistency

  • New methods for all models: coef(), vcov(), logLik(), nobs(), fitted(), residuals() (response and, for countreg(), Pearson), confint(), formula(), terms() and print(). AIC(), BIC() and update() now work. For panel models, logLik() reports the number of panels as its nobs, so BIC() uses the number of independent units.
  • simulate() draws responses from fitted countreg() models (all families, including underreporting).
  • Every estimator stores one covariance matrix (vcov()), and renb(), poisLind.re() and countreg_rp() gain stderr = c("normal", "robust", "boot"). Robust standard errors of panel models are clustered by panel; bootstraps resample whole panels. countreg_rp() gains bootstraps.
  • All estimators gain keep_data; keep_data = FALSE does not store the training data.
  • countreg_rp() and poislind_re() are snake_case names for countreg_rp() and poisLind.re().
  • For fitted models, AIC() and BIC() replace myAIC() and myBIC().

flexCountReg 0.1.1

  • Initial CRAN submission.
